Subject: On-prem observability: proxy capabilities preflight

Hi Aditya,

Quick ask from our side as we get ready to sign the on-prem addendum: Security needs to confirm the observability "evidence" flow from a Redwood private deploy into our SIEM (Splunk Cloud in our VPC). High-level checklist below — can your team confirm support and any gaps?

- Can the on-prem proxy stream logs (application + system), metrics (Prometheus remote write), and tracing spans into our Splunk HEC endpoint inside the VPC?
- Do you support mTLS client certs from the proxy to customer endpoints (we require two-way TLS for HEC)?
- Token/key rotation: can HEC tokens or certs be rotated without dropping buffered events?
- Can Redwood produce a signed "evidence manifest" per export (hashes + schema) we can ingest for audit?
- Can you support PII redaction or deterministic hashing at the exporter if required?
- Retention metadata: can the exporter attach TTL / retention labels to each bundle/event?

We're happy to share our requirement spreadsheet (attached) and can schedule a short technical run-down. Can you loop in the engineer who owns the on-prem proxy?

Thanks,
Alex Jenkins
Head of Security, Acme Inc.

Adding technical detail so Alex has a sense of the concrete knobs we'll exercise during the validation.

Notes / constraints (short):
- Transport: our exporter supports HTTPS POST to HEC with mTLS (client cert) and/or HEC token header. We recommend mTLS when the HEC endpoint lives in customer VPC.
- Buffering & rotation: the proxy uses persistent local spool (disk-backed) with at-least-once delivery semantics. Token/cert rotation is supported via a hot-swap path: new certs/tokens staged in a separate file path, switchover done atomically; spool continues to drain to destination endpoint. We will validate that large spools do not cause timeouts.
- Manifest signing: we produce a JSON manifest per batch containing: bundle_id, exported_signal_types, baseline_hash (sha256), timestamp, retention_label. Signatures are produced using the customer's KMS (if provided) or default Redwood signing key; customers can request signed manifests only with their KMS.
- PII handling: support for deterministic hashing at source (configurable per-field) + a redaction pipeline that strips matching regexes. Note: hashing is irreversible — we will document the fields and a hashing salt policy.
- Header preservation: we can include trace-context headers and original host headers as metadata fields (configurable) so Splunk can correlate logs/traces.

Suggested validation cases for the call:
1) mTLS to HEC: cert auth + HEC token fallback
2) Token rotation test during steady-state (inject rotation event)
3) Manifest verification: generate signed manifest and validate hash in Splunk ingestion job
4) PII hashing: sample payload with sensitive fields -> verify hashing and downstream correlation works (trace id preserved)

I'm adding a small snippet you can paste into the proxy deployment for the test (high level):

- proxy.config.export.hec.endpoint: https://splunk-hec.acme.internal:8088/services/collector
- proxy.config.transport.mtls: true
- proxy.config.auth.cert_path: /var/lib/redwood/certs/acme-client.pem
- proxy.config.manifest.signer: kms://projects/acme/kms/key-1 (optional)

I'll bring a local script to simulate rotation and to populate the spool.
